itinerary.cal: Climbed June to September; early season the gully holds snow and wants an ice axe and possibly crampons, while mid-to-late summer it is rubble. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park, and the climb is done car to car in one day.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day car-to-car outing: roughly 2.5 miles and 1,900 ft up the Blue Lake Trail and climbers' path, about six pitches up the chasm between the Early Winters Spires, four single-rope rappels and the walk out.

days.title: Approach, climb and rappel the Chockstone
days.objective: Summit North Early Winters Spire and return to the car
days.note: Follow the Blue Lake Trail about two miles to the second meadow, then the carabiner-marked climbers' path left to the west face, about 2.5 miles and 1,900 ft to the base (about 1 hr 15 min for one party). The 5.7 crux passes the giant chockstone on the left, a 5.0 ramp turns a second chockstone, and loose 5.4 chimneys lead to a 3rd/4th-class summit scramble; descend four bolted 60 m rappels plus a tree rappel down the starting slab. Day totals use the row's 5,400 ft trailhead and 7,760 ft summit; the hours figure is an estimate built from the approach time and route length, not a reported car-to-car time.

notes: Mountain Project's approach page gives 2.5 mi and 1,913 ft gain to the base; the row's 2,350 ft is consistent as trailhead-to-summit. The row's 1-2 hr approach matches the 1 hr 15 min reported for the neighbouring Northwest Corner. No source gave a car-to-car time for this exact route, so the 8 hours is an estimate. MP lists the route as 600 ft and 6 pitches; gethighonaltitude calls it about 1,000 ft and gives the summit as 7,807 ft against the row's 7,760 ft.

itinerary.cal: Best in June and July, while the face holds firm snow and the bergschrund crossings are still easy. A Mount Rainier climbing permit and wilderness camping permit are required. Most parties take three days with one or two camps, and fast teams have done it in a two-day push.
itinerary.totalNote: A three-day carry-over: hike in to a camp on lower Ptarmigan Ridge, climb the Central Mowich Face to Liberty Cap and drop down the Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman, then walk out to White River (this ends at a different trailhead, so plan a car shuttle).

days.title: Mowich Lake to lower Ptarmigan Ridge
days.objective: Reach a camp on lower Ptarmigan Ridge
days.note: Take the Wonderland and Spray Park trail about 4 miles to Spray Park, then the climbers' trail up lower Ptarmigan Ridge to around 8,200-8,600 ft. Parties have camped on the ridge above Observation Rock (8,600 ft) or dropped right away to an 8,100 ft camp on the Edmunds Glacier divide. Gain is derived from the 4,955 ft trailhead to about 8,300 ft; the mileage is approximate.

days.title: Central Mowich Face to Liberty Cap
days.objective: Climb the face and carry over to Camp Schurman
days.note: Drop about 1,000 ft from the ridge onto the North Mowich Glacier and cross under the ice-cliff runout early. The face runs at about 40-47 degrees, steepening to 50-60 degree ice on the harder upper variation, to the top of the face at about 13,400 ft, then onto Liberty Cap. Descend the Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman (about 9,500 ft). Gain and loss are derived from row elevations: about 8,300 ft to 7,300 ft, up to 14,112 ft, then down to Schurman.

schedule.label: Wake
schedule.detail: From a camp at about 8,100 ft below the face.

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Up to the bergschrund on the North Mowich Glacier.

schedule.label: Top of the face
schedule.detail: About 13,400 ft after roughly 42-47 degree snow.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Columbia Crest by way of Liberty Cap, for a ski party; climbers on harder ice have taken up to 12 hours to Liberty Cap.

days.title: Camp Schurman to White River
days.objective: Descend the Emmons and Inter Glacier to the trailhead
days.note: Descend from Camp Schurman by the Emmons/Inter Glacier and the Glacier Basin trail to White River. Loss is derived from about 9,500 ft to the roughly 4,400 ft trailhead; the mileage is approximate.

notes: The schedule comes from a 2016 three-day ski ascent (turns-all-year) that returned down the face to Mowich Lake rather than carrying over. Alpinedave (2002) approached from the West Side Road, carried over the Disappointment Cleaver and took 12 hours from camp to Liberty Cap with a 2-hour detour. A search snippet of a 2019 CascadeClimbers report (the page itself returned 403) describes a two-day push from Mowich Lake to White River by the Emmons, which supports the row's descent. The row's 6,200 ft gain is roughly camp-to-summit; trailhead to summit is about 9,150 ft. Day mileages are approximations allocated to match the 27.36 km (17 mi) traverse total on the sibling North Mowich Headwall row.

itinerary.cal: An early-season objective, roughly June to early July: the hourglass icefall on the headwall can be completely melted out by August. A Mount Rainier climbing permit and wilderness camping permit are required; plan three days.
itinerary.totalNote: A three-day carry-over that shares the Mowich Face approach: camp on lower Ptarmigan Ridge, climb the North Mowich Headwall to Liberty Cap and descend the Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman, then walk out to White River (this needs a car shuttle).

days.title: Mowich Lake to lower Ptarmigan Ridge
days.objective: Reach a camp on lower Ptarmigan Ridge
days.note: Take the Wonderland and Spray Park trail about 4 miles to Spray Park, then the climbers' trail up lower Ptarmigan Ridge to around 8,300 ft. Parties have camped above Observation Rock at 8,600 ft. Gain is derived from the 4,955 ft trailhead; the mileage is approximate.

days.title: North Mowich Headwall to Liberty Cap
days.objective: Climb the headwall and carry over to Camp Schurman
days.note: Descend scree to the North Mowich Glacier (aim for a snow finger near 8,200 ft rather than dropping lower), then climb toward the headwall, where the crux is an ice hourglass that can be out of condition late in the season. Bivy sites exist at about 9,200 ft and just below the headwall near 10,000 ft for parties who split this day. Continue to Liberty Cap and descend the Emmons-Winthrop to Camp Schurman; gain and loss are derived from row elevations.

days.title: Camp Schurman to White River
days.objective: Descend to the White River trailhead
days.note: Descend from Camp Schurman by the Emmons/Inter Glacier and the Glacier Basin trail. Loss is derived from about 9,500 ft to the roughly 4,400 ft trailhead.

notes: No dedicated trip report for the North Mowich Headwall could be opened; SummitPost returned 403. The plan relies on the shared Mowich-side approach and camps (upwardescape 2012 found the headwall icefall out of shape in August and used a snow ramp instead, with camps at 8,600 ft and about 10,000 ft) and on the row's Emmons descent. The row's 9,200 ft gain matches trailhead to summit (4,955 to 14,112 ft). Its 27.36 km fits a one-way Mowich Lake to White River traverse, not a round trip; the day miles are approximations allocated to that total.

itinerary.cal: Best mid-July to mid-September, when the glacier crossing and moat at the base are manageable; the Direct is often done earlier in the season. A free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is required. Parties often plan two days, but three is the more relaxed plan.
itinerary.totalNote: A three-day plan: hike from Pete Lake Trailhead to the big-boulder bivy below the Chimney Glacier, spend a long day on the 9-10 pitch East Face Direct with many rappels, and hike out (fit parties compress this to two days with a headlamp walk-out).

days.title: Pete Lake Trailhead to the boulder bivy
days.objective: Reach the hanging basin below the Chimney Glacier
days.note: Hike a nearly flat 4 miles to Pete Lake, continue on the Lemah Meadow trail to the PCT, and go about half a mile north. Leave the PCT at the second switchback and head northwest to cross the North Fork of Lemah Creek at about 3,380 ft. Then follow the flagged boot path steeply to the big boulder bivy at about 4,600-4,800 ft, which one party reached in 4.5 hours and another in 6.5 hours. Gain is derived from the 2,800 ft trailhead to the 4,800 ft bivy, and the mileage comes from the 7-8 mi reported for the walk out.

days.title: Climb the East Face Direct
days.objective: Summit Chimney Rock and return to camp
days.note: Follow the Class 2 ridge west of camp, cross a snow basin and a saddle near 6,400 ft onto the glacier, and cross the moat to the base at about 6,600 ft. The route has 9-10 pitches of mostly low fifth class with a crux of about 5.4-5.6, and a final deep chimney to the summit. Descend by 8-13 single-rope rappels plus downclimbing, then about 2 hours of talus back to camp. Gain is derived from 4,800 to 7,727 ft; the mileage is an estimate.

schedule.label: Wake
schedule.detail: At the basin bivy, about 4,600 ft.

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Class 2 east ridge, snow basin, notch and saddle to the upper glacier.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 7,727 ft, about 6 hr 20 min from camp.

schedule.label: Off the rappels
schedule.detail: Eight 60 m rappels plus downclimbing took just over 2 hours.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: After almost 2 hours of talus and scree.

days.title: Hike out to Pete Lake Trailhead
days.note: Descend the boot path to the creek crossing, rejoin the PCT, and walk the long, flat trail past Pete Lake to the car; one party took about 3.5 hours from the bivy.

notes: Both opened reports did the climb in two days with a headlamp hike-out the evening of the summit day; the three-day split follows the row's bivy note and the Mountaineers recommendation (seen only in a search snippet; the page returned 403), which gives 16 mi round trip and 4,900 ft gain. These days sum to about 18 mi and 4,950 ft. Pitch counts vary: Lemke reports 10 pitches and 13 rappels, Mountain Project 7 pitches, and the row 9. Sverdina's bivy was at 4,600 ft, versus 4,800 ft in the row.

itinerary.cal: A cold-season mixed route, best roughly March to May when the north-face ice is in. The first ascent was in early April. No climbing or overnight permit is needed in the Mount Baker Wilderness, and registering is voluntary. The first ascent was done car to car in one long day, and the Hogsback camp is the option for splitting it.
itinerary.totalNote: A single long car-to-car day: the Heliotrope Ridge trail and about 4,000 ft of the Coleman Glacier to the base, roughly 300 m of M5R/AI4+ in four or five pitches, then the walk-off down the back of Colfax and the Coleman.

days.title: Climb Kimchi Suicide Volcano car to car
days.objective: Climb the route, walk off and return to the car
days.note: Gain about 1,000 ft through forest on the Heliotrope Ridge trail to the Hogsback (6,000 ft, about 3 miles), then skin or boot about 4,000 ft up the Coleman Glacier to the base near 8,000 ft. The route is about 300 m with a short unprotected M5 move on pitch 1 and a chimney-tunnel on pitch 4, then easy snow and ice to the summit. Walk off the back via the Coleman-Deming side. Gain is the row's 5,790 ft, and the round-trip mileage is an estimate built from the 3-mile trail plus the glacier.

schedule.label: Leave the car
schedule.detail: Up the Heliotrope Ridge trail, then skins on the Coleman Glacier.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Roughly 6 hours on five roped pitches.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Walked off the back of Colfax.

notes: The timing comes from the April 2015 first ascent (Haley/Hart), which drove all the way to the trailhead. Alpinist notes that a snowed-in road would have added about 10 miles and 2,500 ft. Haley's own write-up describes four belayed pitches plus simul-climbing, while Alpinist says five roped pitches. The 10-mile round trip is an estimate, as no source gives the mileage.

But CascadeClimbers returned 403, and no opened source gives the approach distance or a day timeline, so day mileage would be invented. A rerun with access to the 2021 CC trip report (topic 104100) could fill this.

The Mountain Project Cutthroat Peak pages (South Buttress, North Ridge, The Swarm) describe the shared approach from the pullout 1.5 mi west of Washington Pass, but none gives approach time, distance or car-to-car timing, and no second independent source could be opened (search budget exhausted).

Mountain Project gives pitch beta (8 pitches, 5.11c/d, first ascent 2023), the approach as for the North Ridge, and the descent by the South Buttress humps or the West Ridge, but no timing or distance. No second source was found for this new route.
